title: Read a real HTTP response and collect every page safely
sources: Python 3.14 Standard Library: urllib.request.urlopen/Request, http.server, json and urllib.parse; RFC 9110 HTTP semantics; reviewed 2026-10-03
masterChecklist: Sockets, HTTP concepts, REST APIs, requests, retries, idempotency, pagination, rate limits, error handling
whyItMatters: An HTTP response can be incomplete, malformed, unexpectedly large or only one page of many. A client needs explicit boundaries before trusting the data.
simpleExplanation: An HTTP request asks a server for a resource; the response has a status, headers and body. A GET for course records may return only one page plus a next cursor. Set a timeout so waiting has a limit, check the response's content type, cap bytes before JSON parsing, validate the JSON shape and follow only allowed next-page values. Stop after a known maximum number of pages to prevent loops. A status error or invalid body should become a clear failure, not silently look like an empty course list. The companion script runs a tiny HTTP server on 127.0.0.1 and calls it with urllib.request, so it tests a real request without any third-party site. The current browser lesson editor does not run Python or open a local server; its guided data-shape lab is an in-site exercise with a local-script follow-up.
mentalModel: A page is one box in a shipment. Check the label and box size, unpack its items, and follow only a valid next-box number; never assume the first box is the whole shipment.
outcomes: Distinguish response metadata from JSON body data.
Set timeout and maximum body/page limits.
Use an offline loopback fixture for HTTP integration without external learning links.

realWorldExample.scenario: An internal LearnVerse catalog importer fetches paginated course names.
realWorldExample.riskWithoutSetup: It imports only page one, loops forever on a bad cursor or accepts an HTML error page as JSON.
realWorldExample.professionalApproach: Pin a trusted service origin, enforce response limits, validate each page, log safe errors, and test the client against local success/error fixtures before any real deployment.

explanation: This pure function isolates pagination logic from network I/O, so the learner can reason about the shape in the site's guided editor.
Every page must be a mapping with a list of items; a missing or malformed page raises a clear error.
Only known next-page values are accepted, and a three-page cap prevents an unbounded loop.
The companion local_http_demo.py file supplies a real loopback HTTP server and urllib client with timeout, content-type and byte-size checks; the pure example does not pretend to be an HTTP request.
workedExample.safeExperiment: Set the first page's next value to 99 or remove page two and predict which validation error appears. For the actual HTTP boundary, run the saved companion script locally.

procedure: Define the trusted origin, endpoint, page/cursor schema and success/error contract.
Set explicit connection/read timeout and a maximum response size at the HTTP boundary.
Check status/content type, decode JSON and validate expected fields.
Follow only validated next cursors with a maximum page count.
Test success, malformed body, invalid cursor, timeout and status errors against local fixtures; do not silently convert failures to empty results.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming one response contains every record.
commonMistakes.why: The server may split a collection into pages.
commonMistakes.avoid: Follow a documented next cursor until completion with a maximum page count.

commonMistakes.mistake: Calling json.loads on unlimited bytes or an HTML error body.
commonMistakes.why: The body may be large or not the expected format.
commonMistakes.avoid: Check metadata and cap bytes before decoding and validating.

commonMistakes.mistake: Following any next URL from untrusted JSON.
commonMistakes.why: A malicious or broken response could send the client to an unexpected host or loop.
commonMistakes.avoid: Pin the origin and validate cursor format and bounds.

lab.title: Collect two local pages without losing or looping
lab.safety: The in-site exercise uses only provided dictionaries. The optional companion script serves 127.0.0.1 only and makes no external request; the site editor itself is not a Python executor.

simulation.prompt: Page one says next=2, but page two is missing. What should the importer do?
choices: Return page-one items as if complete
Raise a clear missing/invalid page error
Keep requesting pages without a limit
simulation.explanation: An absent required page is a failure, not successful completion; silently returning partial data is misleading.

guidedSteps: Iterate at most three pages, starting at page one.
Reject a missing page or an items field that is not a list.
Append items and return when next is None.
Reject an invalid or self-repeating next page.
Assert the two-page result and test one missing-page failure.
checks: Rejects missing/malformed pages rather than returning partial success.
Does not follow arbitrary external URLs.
hints: if not isinstance(response.get('items'), list): raise ValueError(...)
Use a bounded for loop and return only when next is None.
lab.solutionExplanation: The pure pagination logic returns only after an explicit terminal page and surfaces missing data. The saved local HTTP fixture exercises the actual urllib timeout/header/body boundary separately.
challenges: Predict the failure when next points back to the current page.
Find the bug if a missing page is treated as an empty terminal page.
Experiment locally with the companion loopback server and explain why Content-Type and byte caps are checked before parsing.

projectConnection.milestone: Collect the complete local course catalog through a validated paginated client boundary.
projectConnection.definitionOfDone: Success includes every page; malformed/oversized/unexpected responses are visible failures; the HTTP integration test needs no third-party site.

assessment.question: Why set a maximum number of pages?
assessment.answer: To stop a broken or malicious cursor from causing an unbounded loop.
assessment.explanation: Completion still requires an explicit terminal page.

assessment.question: Can the client treat missing page two as complete?
Why check Content-Type and body size before JSON parsing?
assessment.answer: The response might be an error page or unexpectedly large.
assessment.explanation: Validate the boundary before trusting a body.
